body:
[aida:advisor] OPERATIONAL, NEEDS YOUR CALL: the live drain is running a binary that predates four merged fixes, including two of the specs it is currently failing on.

THE FACTS, verified not inferred:

    .aida/drain.lock   pid 2179516, binary_sha b09197ab72, started 2026-09-21T00:03:29Z (17:03 local)
    on main since that sha:
        9d0951b53d  fix(orchestrator): surface watchdog-stopped work   (BUG-1450, PR #2038)
        066c4ceacb  fix(review): make reviewer verdict provenance enforceable (BUG-1467, PR #2037, merged 17:00:35)
        eb10921231  test(drain): non-blocking PR verdict does not arm the guard (BUG-1495, PR #2036)
        4fd51c96a9  fix(pull): report stranded forge lookup failures    (BUG-1432, PR #2024)

The drain STARTED AT 17:03, three minutes AFTER BUG-1467 merged at 17:00:35, and does not contain it. Nobody rebuilt between the merge and the launch.

My own binary is the same one - 0.15.0, built 15:02:31, sha b09197ab72+dirty - and so is the reviewer's. All three seats and the drain are on one stale build.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DEGRADED RIGHT NOW. BUG-1467 made the verdict handshake record its head sha. Without it, every `--pr` verdict the drain's reviewers write lands with no reviewed_sha - confirmed on PR-2038, PR-2039 and PR-2040, all recorded after the fix merged, all missing it. Those are the handshake files the orchestrator reads to decide whether to proceed. BUG-1450's fix is about surfacing watchdog-stopped work, and BUG-1450 is itself sitting `failed` in this drain's member list.

Three of the batch's members are failed: BUG-1450 PR-2038, BUG-1452 PR-2039, BUG-1454 PR-2040. Two of those are the fixes that are not running.

THE CALL IS YOURS AND I AM NOT TAKING IT. A live wave pins its launcher binary, `make build-fast` refuses to replace it, and `AFTER_WAVE=1` parks until QueueDrained. Stopping a drain at depth 2 mid-batch to rebuild is a throughput decision, not an integrity one, and it is yours. The options as I see them:

  a. Let the wave finish, then rebuild before the next one. Costs: verdicts recorded for the rest of this batch carry no sha, so the merge-time provenance gate has nothing to compare on them, and they join the 468-of-543 shaless corpus.
  b. Drain-stop after the current spec, rebuild, relaunch. Costs a restart and whatever STORY-1391 has in flight.

I lean (b) only if this batch has many specs left to review. If it is nearly done, (a) is fine and the cleanup is a re-record.

WHAT I WOULD LIKE REGARDLESS, and it is the durable half. Nothing on the path of a running command reports this. `aida --version` and `aida dev status` are both honest if asked, and neither is asked. The MCP server ALREADY self-respawns when the on-disk binary reports a newer sha - that mechanism exists and is simply not applied to the drain launcher or the CLI. A drain that compared its own binary sha against origin/main HEAD at launch and refused, or warned loudly, would have caught this at 17:03.

And the structural point, which is the reviewer's and is good: the seat most likely to be running a stale binary is the seat that just merged the fix, because merging is what makes their build stale. The output looks identical either way, so the seat whose work the fix governs is the one least able to see it is not in effect.
subject: Live drain is running a pre-17:00 binary - four merged fixes not in effect, including two of the specs it is failing on
